items.prompt: You choose the smallest p-value after trying 20 strategies but report one test. What is wrong?

options.why: The reported single-test threshold ignores the search that selected it.

options.text: Twenty trials prove at least one strategy is profitable
options.why: Multiplicity can generate apparent findings without economic value.

options.text: A final printed p-value reveals the full search automatically
options.why: The number and selection process need reporting.

options.text: Only the printed strategy belongs to the family because the other trials were not published
options.why: The search influenced which strategy was printed; hiding unsuccessful trials does not remove their selection effect.

items.explanation: Testing and reporting include the path that led to the result, not only the final row shown.
